decision_user: Meridian Foundation investment committee, advised by the CIO
decision: Decide whether to authorize further analysis and a small pilot; do not execute trades from this record
objective: Policy goal: pursue CPI plus 4% net of estimated costs over rolling five-year periods. Optimization objective is unresolved; any Lab 14 allocation is a mechanics-only classroom probe until the CIO chooses the measurable tradeoff.
benchmark: 60% broad global equities / 40% U.S. investment-grade bonds
risk_measure: Calendar-year total-return loss relative to the CIO's stated 10% threshold, supplemented provisionally by annualized volatility, drawdown, distribution coverage, and benchmark-relative risk; enforcement rule and acceptable probability require clarification
constraints: Long-only; no borrowing, short sales, or derivatives
Keep at least $3,000,000, equal to twelve months of scheduled distributions, in cash or daily-liquid government securities
At least 90% of the portfolio must be redeemable within five business days under ordinary market conditions
Annual turnover should not exceed 25% unless the committee approves a documented exception
Quarterly review and annual rebalancing over the seven-year policy horizon
Evaluate the CPI plus 4% objective net of estimated costs over rolling five-year periods
Do not treat the statement that calendar-year loss cannot exceed 10% as an enforceable guarantee until the CIO defines the rule, probability, and breach response
No sector, climate, social, tax, active-management, or home-bias preference may be invented
validation_tests: Benchmark test: compare return and risk with the 60/40 policy benchmark
Naive-baseline test: compare with equal weight and inverse-volatility allocations
Covariance test: verify labels, units, symmetry, unit correlation diagonal, nonnegative variances, and positive semidefiniteness
Constraint audit: verify sum to one, long-only, no leverage, issuer cap, liquidity reserve, five-day redemption share, and turnover rule
Perturbation test: prestate direction, then vary expected returns, covariance or correlation, and a material bound one at a time
Holdout rule: no holdout exists for course-authored point-in-time inputs; if historical observations are later introduced, freeze a dated out-of-sample window before fitting
Cost test: deduct estimated trading and implementation costs and test compliance with the 25% turnover default
Distribution test: verify twelve months of scheduled $750,000 quarterly payments remain covered by eligible liquid assets
Failure rule: reject adoption if any hard constraint fails, the recommendation is unstable to plausible perturbations, or the CIO objective remains unresolved
unresolved_ambiguity: Which measurable tradeoff should govern the pilot: probability of achieving CPI plus 4% net of costs, tracking error versus 60/40, drawdown or calendar-year loss risk, probability of meeting distributions, or another objective? The CIO must also define how the 10% calendar-year loss statement is measured and what happens after a breach.
